name: Dark, tense ambient underscore that sits under TV dialogue, arranged in sections that change every 8 bars (intro, build, breakdown, climax, outro): a reverbed pad plus a quiet sub-boom hit every 2 bars, an intro grown by opening a low-pass filter, a 16th-note pluck pulse faded in, home-made whooshes (resampled synth note, chopped, faded in, filter opening, plate tail) as riser-and-impact glue, octave-up doubling for builds, a left/right pair of complementary hits on a shared reverb, a pulsing bass in the breakdown, denser hits in the climax and a mirrored fading outro
goal: Write an unobtrusive but tense dark ambient cue meant to sit under dialogue (think minimal, ominous sci-fi film scoring). Set markers so the section changes every 8 bars. Intro: a pad with a plate reverb recorded as a long chord, a sub-boom impact every 2 bars kept quiet, a sustained bass note, a low-pass filter automated from dark to open while raising the patch brightness so the intro grows into the next section, a textural layer on the second half, and a 16th-note pluck pulse whose volume fades in. Glue each section edge with a rise and an impact: a quiet stock whoosh aligned to the beat, or a home-made whoosh (render a low synth note, chop it, fade it in, automate a low-pass opening and add a plate tail with longer decay). Build: remove the intro filter automation so the full spectrum plays, double notes an octave up, add a sustained melodic layer with its highs filtered (bring highs back later), raise notes of the pulse/arp an octave, duplicate without overthinking. Add new hits every 2 bars; duplicate a hit track with a different sound panned to the other side and send both through the same reverb for width. Breakdown: make the bass pulse rhythmically (shaper/tremolo automation on), reintroduce a texture briefly, bring back single-note pulses, a resampled clap, and a heavy synth note with falling pitch automation (braam-like). Climax: copy the build, add the breakdown layers, hits every 2 bars instead of every 4, a long high string note doubled an octave up for the second half, a 2-bar riser (pitched down if too bright, time-stretched), and a quiet low eighth-note percussion pulse. Outro: copy the intro and reverse the moves (fade and close instead of opening), fading the hits out.

prerequisites: A DAW with markers, freeze/render-in-place, fades and filter automation
A pad synth, a pluck, a bass and a string sound
Impact/sub-boom hits and a plate reverb; optional tape/wow plug-in

inputs.name: key_or_root
inputs.description: Root note for the pad and sustained bass

inputs.name: section_bars
inputs.description: Bars per section (8 in the video)

outputs.name: stems
outputs.description: Pad, pulse, hits, risers, bass stems for editing under picture

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Underscore rule: nothing intrusive; keep hits, whooshes and risers turned well down so dialogue sits on top.
The speaker's tape 'wear' warble on strings is optional for unease; Matt prefers steady pitch, so leave it off or keep it very subtle.
Matt prefers a pulse early: the sub-boom every 2 bars and the faded-in 16th pluck start in the intro, so there is no long beatless opening.
Commercial libraries and plug-ins in the video are mapped to generic pad, pluck, impact and riser sources; render your own whooshes instead of using library ones where possible.

steps.action: Set markers so the section changes every 8 bars: intro, build, breakdown, climax, outro.
Intro: record a long pad chord with plate reverb; add a quiet sub-boom impact every 2 bars and a sustained bass note.
steps.expect: A dark bed with a slow pulse of impacts.

steps.action: Put a low-pass filter on the pad and automate it from dark to open across the intro; raise the patch brightness so it opens further by the section end.
steps.expect: The intro grows into the build.

steps.action: Add a texture layer on the second half of the intro and a 16th-note pluck pulse quantized and faded in by volume automation.
steps.expect: A rhythmic motif appears without a hard entrance.

steps.action: At each section edge add a rise and an impact: a quiet whoosh aligned to the beat, or render a low synth note, chop it, fade it in, automate a low-pass opening and add a plate tail with a longer decay.
steps.expect: Sections are glued by a home-made riser into a hit.

steps.action: Build: drop the intro filter so the pad is full-spectrum, double it an octave up, add a sustained melodic layer with its highs filtered, and move some pulse/arp notes up an octave; duplicate the build blocks.
steps.expect: More frequencies and register without new material.

steps.action: Add new hits every 2 bars; duplicate the hit track with a different hit panned to the opposite side and group both into one shared reverb.
steps.expect: A wide, complementary left/right impact pair.

steps.action: Breakdown: switch the bass from sustained to rhythmically pulsing (tremolo/shaper automation on), bring back the texture briefly and the single-note pulses, add a resampled clap and a heavy synth note with falling pitch automation; hits every 4 bars.
steps.expect: A more intense but sparse middle section.

steps.action: Climax: copy the build, add breakdown elements, hits every 2 bars, a long high string note doubled an octave up for the second half, a 2-bar riser (pitch it down or time-stretch if needed) and a quiet low eighth-note percussion pulse.
Outro: copy the intro and mirror it: filter closing and fading instead of opening, hits fading out; then do a quick mix pass.
steps.expect: The cue resolves in reverse of how it began.

verification: Section boundaries fall every 8 bars and each one has a riser or whoosh into an impact.
Hit density goes from every 2 bars (intro/build) to every 4 (breakdown) to every 2 again (climax).
Outro automation is the reverse of the intro automation.
